entities.summary:
Benedetto Buglioni (1459/1460–1521) was a renowned Italian Renaissance sculptor who specialized in glazed terracotta, creating intricate and ornate pieces that showcased his mastery of the medium.

Buglioni's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Renaissance art, particularly in the field of terracotta sculpture. His work can be seen in various museums and galleries across Italy, including the Uffizi Gallery in Florence and the Vatican Museums in Rome.

Buglioni's legacy extends beyond his artistic achievements, as he played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and artistic landscape of Italy during the Renaissance. His work influenced many artists, including Michelangelo and Raphael, and helped to establish Italy as a hub for artistic innovation.

In his later years, Buglioni was particularly fascinated by the art of glazing terracotta, experimenting with new techniques and materials to create even more intricate and detailed designs.

Buglioni's life and work serve as a testament to the enduring power of art to shape and reflect the culture and values of a society.
